gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-tc: Commanding, bent-rod letters from Righteous, with bowls that fill the line. Noto Sans TC is the friendlier sans below, its large open counters and outward-opening curves making paragraphs feel unhurried.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-thai-looped: Righteous looks like thin steel rod bent into letters, with zero stroke modulation. It earns its keep big and short, while Noto Sans Thai Looped, a sans-serif with tall bodies and spacious curve terminals, handles the rest.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-tifinagh: Fun, glass-tubing letters come from Righteous, with bowls filling the line. Where Righteous commands attention at display size, Noto Sans Tifinagh keeps inflated, rounded letters open and inviting as sans-serif body text.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Commanding and hairline-free, Righteous bends every letter like thin steel rod. Noto Sans Tirhuta, a sans-serif with cut-back terminals and a dominant x-height, can sit at a modest size without losing its openness.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-vithkuqi: Fun and commanding, Righteous keeps its strokes smooth, with no pinching at curves. Beneath it, Noto Sans Vithkuqi keeps open throats and a minimal cap-to-lowercase step, so the handoff from loud heading to sans text feels smooth.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Hulking, chalk-pressed lowercase reads loud beneath Righteous, which has zero stroke contrast. Noto Sans Wancho, its e carrying a wide gap at its terminal, supplies the sturdy, contemporary punch.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-warang-citi: Noto Sans Warang Citi sets words as solid blocks beneath Righteous and its hairline-free a. Noto Sans Warang Citi's wide channels lead into each counter, so paragraphs of sans-serif text move along smoothly.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-yi: Righteous bends thin steel rod into letters whose crossbars match their stems. Noto Sans Yi, with a deep lowercase midsection and rounds left unlatched like a hook, reads smoothly across paragraphs.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-zanabazar-squ: Noto Sans Zanabazar Square reads open, with a soaring x-height. Righteous, whose strokes never vary in thickness, shouts above it, and the wide gaps in the sans keep small text crisp.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-traditional-nushu: Righteous has no hairline-to-stem shift, just thin steel rod bent into every letter. Noto Traditional Nushu adds a broad-nibbed pen stroke that never curls shut, so the two sit together comfortably.
